Reproduced this in-session behavior again on OpenCode 1.18.18 (official Linux binary), on CachyOS Linux/Wayland inside the Cursor integrated terminal (`TERM=xterm-256color`, `TERM_PROGRAM=vscode`, `COLORTERM=truecolor`). After the provider operation completed normally, moving the mouse filled the prompt with raw SGR movement reports such as `<35;176;6M`, `<35;115;18M`, and `<35;83;23M`. The TUI then appeared unresponsive as continued movement added more input, but the OpenCode process remained alive and the correlated logs had no provider, watcher, snapshot, or MCP warnings/errors.

Mouse was not explicitly configured, so the documented `mouse: true` default applied. OpenCode 1.18.18 uses OpenTUI 0.4.5; with mouse enabled, modes 1000, 1002, 1003, and SGR 1006 are enabled. This looks like a recurrence of mouse input parsing/state desynchronization, potentially triggered by the Cursor/xterm.js + Wayland combination, but I have not isolated whether the fault is in OpenCode, OpenTUI, or the terminal interaction.

Both `OPENCODE_DISABLE_MOUSE=1 opencode` and setting `mouse: false` in `~/.config/opencode/tui.json` (then restarting) avoid the issue.

Same root cause also hits the **free Console tier** (`/zen/v1`), so this is broader than pro-on-Go.

- Client: Codex CLI 0.147.0 (`wire_api = responses`), base `https://opencode.ai/zen/v1`, model `deepseek-v4-flash-free`
- Error: `Error from provider (Console): Upstream request failed: [400] 1 validation error: {'type': 'missing', 'loc': ('body', 'tools', 9, 'function', 'name'), ...}` — sglang upstream, `POST /v1/chat/completions`
- Same config pointed at `/zen/go/v1` + `deepseek-v4-flash` succeeds.
- Chat/completions format with the same tools against `/zen/v1` + `deepseek-v4-flash-free` passes schema validation and only hits the free-tier rate limit (429) — so the tools themselves are accepted; only the responses→chat-completions conversion breaks.

Matches the captured root cause here: the converter mishandles codex's `web_search` tool (which carries an `external_web_access` field) and emits `{"type":"function","function":{}}` with no `name`. A bare `{"type":"web_search"}` probe passes, consistent with the fielded shape being the trigger. Worth retitling to cover the free tier as well, since the PR #40210 fix needs to reach the `/zen/v1` path too.

opencode's chat works like a live news ticker: when the agent generates text, the window slides down to show the latest line. That's good when you're at the bottom. The problem (issue #7659): when you scroll up to read, the window keeps yanking you back down — like a book someone keeps turning pages on.


The chat's auto-scroll is hardcoded via the `<scrollbox>`'s sticky scroll — `stickyScroll={true}` + `stickyStart="bottom"` in [`packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx#L1181-L1182), powered by `@opentui/core`'s `ScrollBox` ([`ScrollBox.ts`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/main/packages/core/src/renderables/ScrollBox.ts)). The TUI config only exposes `scroll_speed` / `scroll_acceleration`, so users can't turn the follow behavior off.


1. **Clamp-based re-stick** — `syncManualScrollState()` reset `_hasManualScroll = false` during content updates (`_isApplyingStickyScroll`). Whenever streamed content momentarily shrank (collapsing tool output, snapshot churn), the scroll position got clamped to the (new) bottom and the view silently re-stuck.
2. **Aggressive re-engage** — `recalculateBarProps()` re-engaged sticky when the user was within **1 line of the bottom** (`scrollTop >= maxScrollTop - 1`), pulling the view past where they were reading.

**The patch (local build `1.xx.xx-localscroll`)**

In `@opentui/core` `ScrollBox`:
- `syncManualScrollState()`: early-return inside `_isApplyingStickyScroll` — no more `_hasManualScroll` reset from content-size clamps.
- `recalculateBarProps()`: removed the `isAtStickyReengagePoint` auto-re-engage branch. Follow now resumes **only** when the user actually scrolls back to the bottom (`syncManualScrollState` on real input handles that).

In opencode TUI:
- `packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx`: `scrollbar_visible` default `false → true` (visible scrollbar = position indicator).

Kept the existing streaming markdown fix. Built from the `v1.xx.xx` tag (`bun run build --single` in `packages/opencode`, `OPENCODE_VERSION=1.xx.xx-localscroll`).

**Resulting behavior**

- At the bottom → viewport follows the latest output.
- Scroll up (even a couple of lines) → scroll stays put; no yanking, even when content temporarily shrinks and clamps the position.
- Scroll back to the very bottom → follow resumes.
- Scrollbar visible by default.

**Suggested upstream change (proper PR)**

Same idea in source:
1. `@opentui/core` `ScrollBox.ts`: apply the two fixes above (remove clamp re-stick + auto re-engage), then add a config flag to opencode's TUI config (e.g. `scroll_sticky: boolean`, default `true`) wired to `stickyScroll` in `session/index.tsx`.

**Links**

- Chat scrollbox: https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/dev/packages/tui/src/routes/session/index.tsx#L1181-L1182
- Sticky-scroll impl (`@opentui/core`): https://github.com/anomalyco/opentui/blob/main/packages/core/src/renderables/ScrollBox.ts
- TUI config docs: https://opencode.ai/docs/tui/

This isn't a memory leak — it's a shutdown race in `@opentui/core`, and there's already a fix sitting upstream that nobody here seems to know about:

- **anomalyco/opentui#1319** — the issue
- **anomalyco/opentui#1318** — the fix (open, unreviewed)

## What's actually happening

`TreeSitterClient.destroy()` rejects every in-flight `highlightOnce()` request in one shot via `rejectPendingRequests()`, which walks the whole `messageCallbacks` map. `CodeRenderable.startHighlight()` catches each rejection and logs it as a genuine highlighting failure — the `console.warn` at `Code.ts:418` runs *before* the `if (this.isDestroyed) return` on the next line.

So the count of warnings tracks the number of queued highlight requests, not anything leaking. That's why it looks worse the longer the session has been running: more rendered code blocks in the transcript, more pending requests to reject.

## Still reproducing on 1.18.18

macOS arm64. The `v1.18.18` tag pins `@opentui/core` `0.4.5`, and the shipped bundle still has the warn ahead of the guard:

```
$ strings -a ~/.opencode/bin/opencode | grep -o 'Code highlighting failed.\{0,120\}'
Code highlighting failed, falling back to plain text:",H),this.isDestroyed)return;this.textBuffer.setText($)...
```

## Two things that may help people triaging this

**It never reaches the log file.** On my machine:

```
$ grep -c "TreeSitter client destroyed" ~/.local/share/opencode/log/opencode.log
0
```

The warnings go straight to the terminal because `finalizeDestroy()` calls `_console.destroy()` → `restoreOriginalConsole()` in the same synchronous block, while the rejections settle on a later microtask — by the time they fire, `global.console` is the original one again. So if you're looking for these in `opencode.log`, they aren't there.

**The warning path itself is renderable-side only** (`console.warn` + `textBuffer.setText`), so it can't touch persistence. On the session I hit this with, all 209 messages were intact in `opencode.db` and `opencode -s <session-id>` resumed fine — the only casualty was the assistant turn that was mid-stream when `Ctrl+C` landed (`cost: 0`, all token counts 0), which just needs re-sending.

FWIW, the "remove MCP servers that can't load" workaround mentioned above addresses a different failure — it doesn't affect this particular stack.

When working with the file tree in the workspace sidebar, I frequently need to operate on the currently selected file/directory. Right now, I have to manually type paths or drag files around, which is slow and error-prone. I'd like a right-click context menu on file tree items that provides quick actions:

Copy Relative Path — copy the path relative to the current workspace root (e.g. src/components/Button.tsx) to the clipboard.
Copy Absolute Path — copy the full absolute path (e.g. D:\projects\my-app\src\components\Button.tsx) to the clipboard.
Reveal in File Explorer — open the system file explorer (Windows Explorer / Finder / Nautilus) and highlight the selected file or directory.
Reference File — insert a file reference (e.g. @src/components/Button.tsx or the file:path syntax used for attachments) directly into the active chat input, so I can easily attach files without dragging them.
These actions are standard in other editors (VS Code, Zed, etc.) and would significantly speed up workflows like referencing files in prompts, sharing paths, and locating files on disk. Multiple selection support (e.g. copying a list of paths when several files are selected) would be a nice bonus.

Adding new evidence that was not in the original report and addressing the byte-identity point raised in #31525.

## Consecutive cache busts (not previously reported)

The most expensive session (`ses_03563ecbdffe92x5KFrsYJRWnN`, $18.66, 43 messages) shows **5 consecutive cache busts** across messages #34-38. Each turn re-wrote ~260K tokens at cache-write pricing ($6.25/M), costing $1.63 per turn:

```
msg#  cache_read  cache_write  cost    prev_finish
34    0           259,313      $1.63   tool-calls
35    0           259,498      $1.63   tool-calls
36    0           259,734      $1.63   tool-calls
37    0           260,018      $1.63   tool-calls
38    0           260,207      $1.63   tool-calls
```

Five consecutive turns, $8.15, zero cache reads. This is not a one-off invalidation; the cache is being re-written on *every* turn during a tool-use loop.

## Full bust pattern (all 9 after tool-calls)

| msg# | cache_write | cost | prev_finish |
|------|-------------|------|-------------|
| 1    | 84,195      | $0.55 | (start) |
| 21   | 233,523     | $1.47 | tool-calls |
| 29   | 255,794     | $1.61 | tool-calls |
| 30   | 256,289     | $1.61 | tool-calls |
| 34-38| 259-260K    | $1.63 x5 | tool-calls (x5) |

9 of 9 busts immediately follow a `tool-calls` finish. The correlation is deterministic, not incidental.

## On the byte-identity framing (#31525)

I understand the objection that Anthropic caching is keyed on content, not object identity. The data here does not depend on that framing. The observable fact is that `cache_read = 0` and `cache_write > 0` on turns immediately after tool-calls, and `cache_write` scales with full context size (~260K tokens), not with the incremental delta. Whatever the exact mechanism, the effect is that the entire conversation is re-serialized into the cache on each tool-turn, and Anthropic charges cache-write rates for it.

## Reproducible from the database

No API introspection required. Anyone can verify from `~/.local/share/opencode/opencode.db`:

```sql
WITH msg_list AS (
  SELECT
    json_extract(data, '$.finish') as finish,
    json_extract(data, '$.tokens.cache.read') as cache_r,
    json_extract(data, '$.tokens.cache.write') as cache_w,
    json_extract(data, '$.cost') as cost,
    ROW_NUMBER() OVER (ORDER BY json_extract(data, '$.time.created')) as rn
  FROM message
  WHERE session_id = 'ses_03563ecbdffe92x5KFrsYJRWnN'
    AND json_extract(data, '$.role') = 'assistant'
)
SELECT m1.rn, m1.cache_r, m1.cache_w, m1.cost, m2.finish as prev_finish
FROM msg_list m1
LEFT JOIN msg_list m2 ON m1.rn = m2.rn + 1
WHERE m1.cache_r = 0 AND m1.cache_w > 0;
```

## Scope and limitations

This is production evidence from OpenCode 1.18.9 with `opencode/claude-opus-5` (max), running the Sisyphus ultraworker agent. Total waste across 3 sessions is $14.82 (39% of spend). I have since switched these workloads to DeepSeek, whose sessions show steady cache-read growth and zero cache-write charges, which isolates the issue to Anthropic's cache-write pricing combined with this behavior.

I am not asking for a specific implementation, only that this be looked at with the deterministic 9/9 tool-call correlation and the 5-consecutive-bust sequence on record. If a fix lands in #14743 or elsewhere, happy to re-run the same workload and provide before/after numbers.

FYI: this PR links #42120 (Closes #42120 in the description, cross-referenced on the issue timeline). The needs:issue label looks like a stale cross-reference index — happy to fix if I am missing something.

The V2 `question` tool is backed by the form service now, so clients should consume the form API rather than the legacy question API.

When the tool asks a question, the server emits `form.created`. The included form has `metadata.kind === "question"`, tool ownership metadata under `metadata.tool`, and fields named `q0`, `q1`, etc.

Pending requests can also be recovered from:

- `GET /api/form/request` for the current location
- `GET /api/session/{sessionID}/form` for one session

Reply with:

```http
POST /api/session/{sessionID}/form/{formID}/reply
Content-Type: application/json

{"answer":{"q0":"Yes","q1":["A","B"]}}
```

A dismissed question uses `POST /api/session/{sessionID}/form/{formID}/cancel`.

`question.asked` and `/api/question/request` belong to the old in-memory question service and are no longer driven by the built-in tool. Their continued presence in the V2 API is stale; we'll remove that unused surface so generated clients no longer advertise it.

## Additional Context: Azure DevOps Remote MCP Server

### Issue Summary
Confirmed the same POST JSON-RPC transport limitation applies to the **Azure DevOps Remote MCP Server** (`https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{organization}`).

### Configuration Tested
```json
{
  "mcp": {
    "ado-remote-mcp": {
      "type": "remote",
      "url": "https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{organization}",
      "enabled": true
    }
  }
}
```

### Observed Behavior
- OpenCode CLI: `ado-remote-mcp SSE error: Non-200 status code (405)`
- HTTP inspection shows: `Allow: POST` header (server rejects GET/SSE)
- The remote MCP endpoint requires POST-based JSON-RPC transport

### Evidence
```bash
$ curl -I https://mcp.dev.azure.com/{organization}
HTTP/1.1 405 Method Not Allowed
Allow: POST
```

### Documentation Note
The [official Microsoft Learn documentation](https://learn.microsoft.com/en-us/azure/devops/mcp-server/remote-mcp-server?view=azure-devops) specifies `"type": "http"` for `.vscode/mcp.json` (VS Code only), but this type is not supported by OpenCode's MCP configuration schema.

### Affected Clients
- OpenCode CLI
- OpenCode (any environment using `opencode.jsonc` config)
- Potentially other tools expecting `type: "remote"` to support SSE

### Workaround
Use `.vscode/mcp.json` configuration for VS Code IDE, or use the local Azure DevOps MCP Server package with OpenCode instead.

### Recommendation
OpenCode MCP `type: "remote"` should either:
1. Support POST-based JSON-RPC transport, or
2. Detect and negotiate transport protocol during handshake (SSE vs POST)

Closing as duplicate of #38787 — same root cause: the runLoop's lexicographic lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id comparison breaks when message IDs are not monotonic. The wrap-around case (2026-08-14, IDs flipping order) is added as a comment on #38787.

Additional corroborating case (from a closed duplicate, #42570):

On 2026-08-14T11:19:55Z the 36-bit embedded timestamp in MessageID wrapped (26 x 2^36 ms). Sessions with messages on both sides of the wrap show the same non-monotonic ordering, but flipped the other way: pre-wrap assistant IDs (msg_ffff...) now sort AFTER the new post-wrap user ID (msg_0001...), so \lastUser.id < lastAssistant.id\ evaluates true and the loop exits at step=0 without any reply — opposite symptom of the duplicate-response case here.
